sentences.text: Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Najakat Ali

Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri Garun Pal Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Najakat Ali, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Rajendra Prasad Singh, learned State Law Officer for the State and perused the record.
2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 257 of 2024, under Sections 376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Jagdishpura, District Agra, during the pendency of trial.

PROSECUTION STORY:
3. The applicant is stated to have seen the daughter of the informant with the boy of the locality, as such had blackmailed her and taken her to a hotel and committed rape with her and had even taken certain indecent photograph of her and kept on blackmailing her.
The offence is stated to have been committed by the applicant on 17.05.2024.
The age of the victim is stated to be 17 years and 9 months.

Pramod vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20024378/
1 ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT :
4. The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has nothing to do with the said offence.
5. The FIR is delayed by about 3 days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
6. The age of the victim as per ossification test report is 18 years.
7. The allegations are per se false as the medical evidence does not support the prosecution story.

entities.text: Pramod vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. The applicant is stated to be the uncle of the victim and the allegations leveled in the FIR are stated to have been made by the victim in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
9.

The victim is a consenting party as is but evident from the statement of the receptionist of the hotel who has stated that the applicant and the victim had come to the hotel on 17.05.2024 and both had told themselves to be husband and wife and stayed in a room for about 45 minutes.
10. The manager of the hotel is stated to have made a statement that the CCTV cameras are non-functional.
11. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
12. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 22.05.2024.
The applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicant is released on bail,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT :
13. The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the applicant is the uncle of the victim and had misused his clout as he was already a married person aged about 30 years.
As such, he is not entitled for bail.

CONCLUSION:
14. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

15. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the Pramod vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20024378/
2 procedure must be just and reasonable.

entities.text: Pramod vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
16.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
17.
Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
18. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

19. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

20. Let the applicant- Pramod involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
21. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

22. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
